description: NLP Prompt Compressor for LLMs. Reduces token usage by up to 70% using semantic contraction across 50+ languages. Licensed under the Caveman License (MIT + mandatory attribution to Passaro Francesco Paolo - Digitalsolutions.it). Bundled language data derived from Universal Dependencies (see NOTICE).
releaseNotes: 1.4.3: re-publish of 1.4.2 -- the previously published 1.4.2 NuGet package was packed from a stale snapshot and was missing the 1.4.0/1.4.1 additions below (CavemanRetriever, CavemanSimHash, CavemanTopicSegmenter, Statistical/Syntactic compression levels). This version contains the full, current feature set. Includes 1.4.2's language-quality pass ported back from the Synthelion (Python port) 1.2.0 quality review. Fixed: negation particles ("non"/"not"/"ne...pas"/"no"/"nicht"/"não"/"不") were being stripped as ordinary function words at every compression level, silently inverting sentence meaning -- now protected in eng/ita/fra/spa/deu/por/zho, with prefix-aware matching for Chinese compounds ("不是"/"不管"). Fixed Italian "subito" (adverb, "immediately") being mis-lemmatised to "subire" (verb, "to undergo") via a UD homograph-contaminated lemma entry -- LemmaOrLower now skips a lemma substitution when the surface form is POS-tagged ADV and the lemma differs. Added CavemanCjkSegmenter: dictionary-based Chinese word segmentation (DAG + dynamic-programming longest-match path, jieba's non-ML dictionary algorithm re-implemented rather than taken as a dependency) -- Chinese previously had no word segmentation at all, so compression and language detection both silently no-op'd beyond punctuation stripping. Repaired real mojibake corruption (UTF-8 mis-decoded as Windows-1252 at an earlier pipeline stage) in worddata/zho.yaml(.br), zho.pos.yaml.br, and _index.br (10 further affected languages: ben, ell, eng, heb, hin, jpn, kor, mar, tha, vie). Fixed language-detection data contamination: "john" (an English name) removed from 16 languages' function-word lists, "ha"/"e" (Italian words, not French) removed from French's list, and "ate" removed from Portuguese's exclusive markers (collided with English's own "ate"). All changes are additive and backward-compatible; 14 new regression tests (311/311 total).
